turns.ask: Our online game's login API keeps getting hammered by massive DDoS attacks. Design the full protection layer and the backend service behind it.

ops.text: I'll design a DDoS-hardened game login API using ESA, Anti-DDoS Proxy, WAF on ALB, and backend services in Singapore.

ops.label: Game players
ops.why: Players calling the login API from clients.

ops.label: Cloud DNS
ops.why: Resolves login domain to ESA CNAME.

ops.label: ESA
ops.why: Caches static assets and provides first-layer DDoS defense at the edge.

ops.label: Anti-DDoS Proxy
ops.why: Scrubs massive L3-L7 DDoS attacks before they reach the origin.

ops.label: ALB
ops.why: Terminates TLS and load-balances login traffic across zones.

ops.label: WAF 3.0
ops.why: Blocks OWASP attacks, CC floods and malicious bots at the ALB.

ops.label: TLS cert
ops.why: Provides the SSL certificate for HTTPS termination.

ops.label: API Gateway
ops.why: Authenticates tokens, rate-limits and routes login API calls.

ops.label: Login servers
ops.why: Runs the game login logic across two zones for HA.

ops.text: Sessions go to Tair and player accounts to RDS, both multi-zone.

ops.label: Session cache
ops.why: Stores login sessions and tokens with low latency.

ops.label: Accounts DB
ops.why: Persists player credentials and profiles with a zone standby.

ops.label: Logs
ops.why: Centralizes access logs and security events for alerting.
